text:
alex: Heads-up — canary deploy for model-serving v2.4 started at 12:04. We intended 5% but the edge LB leak pushed ~20%. Seeing latency spike + quota errors from customers. Need a fast, safe rollback runbook and owner. @sre-oncall

jamal: I can take this. I see routing weight mismatch at the edge (old config vs control-plane). We should 0 the canary weight and drain sessions first.

maria: Agree. Important: drain + evict KV prefix to avoid stale KV hits. If we just drop weight, sticky sessions will keep hitting canary and cause 502s. Also throttle per-route QPS to avoid cascading quota errors.

chris: Proposed quick-swap steps (minimal blast radius):
1) Set canary route weight -> 0 (drain new connections)
2) Enable safe-disable on canary to block new sessions
3) Evict KV prefix used by canary (prefix: canary:) and lower TTLs temporarily
4) Adjust per-route quotas to safe levels (reduce refill)
5) Roll back deployment to v2.3 if weight==0 and active sessions <= 5
6) Monitor traces + token usage + kv hit ratio

chris: Sample commands (run in order):
```bash
# stop new traffic and drain
redwoodctl routes set-weight model-serving-canary 0 --drain-sessions
redwoodctl routes set-flag model-serving-canary safe-disable true

# evict cached prefixes used by canary instances
redwoodctl kv evict --prefix "canary:" --region us-west1 --confirm

# throttle route quotas to avoid quota cascade
redwoodctl quotas set-per-route model-serving 50r/s --window 1s

# rollback once drained
redwoodctl deployment rollback model-serving --to v2.3 --reason "canary-weight-leak"
```

alex: Nice. jamal, can you execute the route weight + safe-disable? I can follow with kv evict. chris, can you prepare the rollback command but hold until we confirm drain metrics?

jamal: On it. Executing weight flip now. Will watch active session count and 502 rate.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: route weight change detected: model-serving-canary weight 5 -> 0 by jamal (tx id: d9f3).

jamal: Weight flip done. Active sessions at ~18 -> draining. 502s started to drop.

maria: I'll run kv evict for prefix and lower TTLs on backup caches. After evict, set a short sticky TTL so new sessions rebind to primary.

infra-bot: kv-bot: evict job queued: prefix=canary:, region=us-west1, job-id=ev-7832.

maria: Evict finished. KV hit ratio for canary prefix down to 2%.

jamal: Active sessions <= 3 now, 502s back to baseline. chris, green to run rollback?

chris: Go for it. Running rollback to v2.3 now. Reason logged: canary-weight-leak.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: rollback started by chris. target=model-serving v2.3, job-id=rb-4410.

alex: Once rollback completes, let's keep a canary-lock on the console to prevent accidental >5% and add an alert for weight divergence between control-plane and edge. Also temporary quota relax to avoid customer-side spike from retries.

sre-oncall: Adding alert rules: 
- canary-config-drift (edge vs control-plane)
- canary-percentage > configured-max
- sudden kv-hit-ratio drop with spike in errors

maria: Follow-up action items:
- investigate root cause of LB config drift (possible race in route propagation)
- add an automated verification step after canary ramp to compare actual edge weights vs intended
- add instrumentation to routing API to surface last-applied-tx in console

alex: Great. jamal/chris/maria — please add the exact commands you ran + logs to the incident ticket. We should also add a short runbook snippet to Console: "fast-swap rollback (route-weight drain + kv-evict)" so on-call can reuse. :thumbsup:

jamal: Will post commands + snippets to the ticket in a minute.

chris: Pushed the rollback run command and captures to #incidents/ticket-1129.

alex: Thanks team — closing thread, tracking follow-ups in the ticket.
